_description: Architectural decision records: routing, state management, build pipeline, major library choices, cross-cutting refactors. Append only; supersede with a new entry instead of editing.

title: Pin TypeScript to 6.0
decision: Pin typescript to the 6.0 line in package.json.
rationale: volar (vue-tsc) and typescript-eslint do not support TS 7 yet.
consequences_negative: Must revisit when tooling supports TS 7.

title: Proxy all GitHub API calls through Nitro with the user OAuth token
context: The app reads and writes the user's GitHub repos from a client-only SPA.
decision: Every GitHub call goes through server/routes/gh-*; the handler reads the token from the nuxt-auth-utils secure session and forwards it as Bearer.
rationale: Secure session data stays server-side, so the GitHub token never reaches the browser; owner is forced to the session user.
consequences_positive: No token in client JS; per-user isolation; zod validation at one trust boundary.
consequences_negative: A Nitro server is required at runtime, so a purely static deploy is not possible.

title: Build the folder layout on Nuxt UI dashboard components
context: The redesign (direction A, 'Finder') needs a persistent vault sidebar, a single header and a mobile drawer for the folder view.
decision: src/layouts/default.vue uses UDashboardGroup + UDashboardSidebar + UDashboardPanel + UDashboardNavbar; vaults render through UNavigationMenu in VaultNavigation.vue.
rationale: Nuxt UI 4 already ships these components with responsive drawer, toggle and theming, so no hand-written shell or extra dependency is needed.
consequences_positive: Sidebar collapse, mobile drawer and spacing come from the library; layout code shrinks.
consequences_negative: Layout markup is tied to Nuxt UI dashboard slots; a library major upgrade may require rework.

title: Detect vault repos by the gitvault GitHub topic, not a marker file
context: Vaults were detected by the gitvault- name prefix, which forces repo names. plan/05 proposed the topic plus a .gitvault marker file in the repo root.
decision: A repo is a vault iff it has the gitvault topic or (transition) the gitvault- name prefix (isVaultRepo in server/resources/gitHubUserRepos.ts). Creation sets the topic with PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/topics right after POST /user/repos. No marker file.
rationale: GET /user/repos already returns topics, so detection costs zero extra calls; a marker file would need a contents/tree call per repo on every list. The prefix fallback keeps existing untagged vaults working without a migration.
consequences_positive: Repo names can become free once the naming UI drops the prefix; no extra API calls on list.
consequences_negative: Creating a vault takes two GitHub calls and can half-fail (repo created, not tagged); the error names the repo. Removing the topic on GitHub hides a non-prefixed vault. The prefix fallback must be removed deliberately later.

title: Gallery backup dedupes by blob sha against the repo tree
context: Users want to back up a phone gallery by re-picking it whole each time, uploading only what is new. Phone file names and dates are unreliable (renames, iOS export dates, IMG_0001 reused across phones).
decision: The backup page (src/pages/[repo]/backup.vue) hashes each picked file client-side as a git blob (sha-1 of 'blob <size>\0' + bytes), skips files whose sha appears anywhere in the gh-repo-tree listing, and queues the rest on the shared useVaultContents upload queue under Photos/YYYY/MM from file.lastModified. Files over MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (src/config.ts) are skipped and listed.
rationale: The tree already carries every blob sha in one request, so dedupe needs no index file, no extra GitHub calls and no new dependency, and it survives renames and moves inside the vault. Reusing the queue keeps one upload pipeline (conflict handling, serial PUTs).
consequences_positive: Re-selecting the whole gallery only uploads new items; moved or renamed files still count as backed up.
consequences_negative: Every file is read fully in memory to hash; a truncated tree (very large repos) misses shas, so those files fall back to the queue's path-conflict prompt. The size cap follows the proxy: the base64 body must fit Netlify's function request limit, so large videos are skipped. The /<repo>/backup route shadows a root folder named backup.
